Paper_name: Accentuate the positive: Evidence that context dependent self-reference drives self-bias
Summary: This research examined the relative primacy of self-bias and positivity-bias using a speeded classification task in which self-relevant information was paired with emotional expressions (Experiment 1) or reward information (Experiment 2). Participants first learned shape-label associations (self, friend, happy, neutral; or self, friend, high reward, low reward) via a shape-label matching task, then completed a classification task in which shapes were paired onto response keys according to condition. When the self was paired with relatively more positive information (smiling faces or high reward), a self-bias but no positivity-bias was observed; when the self was paired with relatively less positive information (neutral faces or low reward), a positivity-bias but no self-bias was observed.
Author: Naomi A. Lee, Douglas Martin, Jie Sui
Conclusion: The relative primacy of prioritised processing is flexible and context dependent: self-bias and positivity-bias trade off depending on what the self is paired with, and the pattern is consistent with a drive towards self-enhancement and the self-positivity bias.
